analysis:
This batch changes documentation only; no implementation source was supplied. In docs/architecture/hardware-support.md, head line 3 updates the date, and head lines 527-554 add a "GDN prompt kernels by GPU" section. In docs/architecture/inference.md, head lines 595-611 document the selection of a four-row Gated DeltaNet prefill kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. Selection uses a per-process probe on a fixed 32-position window and keeps the first candidate that matches gated_delta_step bit for bit. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and windows shorter than 16 positions always use the stock kernel. DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED can restore the stock kernel or force packed or rows.

I compared these changes with the threat model:
- No change to a trust boundary, wire protocol, encryption, attestation, authorization or billing appears.
- Line 552 states that no load quotation, activation floor, KV grant or reported capacity changes. The probe transient is documented as about 16 MiB, so no memory-admission or availability regression is evident under TB-007 or T-029.
- The interaction with prefix-cache checkpoints (T-041) rests on the bit-exactness claim. A probe on one fixed window is evidence for that claim, not proof for all inputs, dtypes or positions.
- The environment option that forces packed or rows is operator-local. The model already treats it as untrusted for output integrity (T-007, T-056). It could let a non-exact kernel write recurrent checkpoints into the same-scope SSD cache. Cache salt scoping remains coordinator-authored and unchanged, so this introduces no cross-account exposure.
- The docs claim at hardware-support.md head line 531 that outputs and checkpoints keep stock bits "on every chip". This is a correctness claim that depends on GatedDelta.swift (GatedDeltaPrefill.probe), which was not supplied.

Integration should verify the following in that source:
- The probe compares outputs and fp32 state exactly.
- Forced kernel modes are excluded from SSD checkpoint donation, or are at least not described as bit-exact.

Neither point is a security regression supported by the evidence here, so I report no findings.
